memory_update.text: Add INST/Instructure as the highest-priority direct public LMS candidate for the learning_infrastructure_lms_security node.
Add PSO/Pearson as a direct assessment-integrity and proctoring candidate tied to online learning, certification, and AI-cheating pressures.
Add WDAY/Workday as a higher-education SIS/ERP modernization candidate, but label exposure as diluted by broader enterprise cloud revenue.

Identity and access management appears to be a plausible second-order chokepoint because education SaaS breaches often involve compromised credentials and large lifecycle populations of students, faculty, staff, applicants, alumni, and parents.

PowerSchool, Ellucian, Anthology/Blackboard, D2L Brightspace, Respondus, Honorlock, ProctorU/Meazure, and Infinite Campus are highly relevant but appear private, foreign-listed, or otherwise not straightforward US-listed common-stock candidates for this pass.

node: Learning management systems, campus software, identity, assessment, and cybersecurity
summary: Expanded universe for the learning-infrastructure/security node. The strongest direct public-market candidates are Instructure for Canvas LMS, Pearson for assessment/proctoring, Workday for higher-education SIS/ERP, Okta for identity access management, and CrowdStrike for cybersecurity/incident-response exposure. PowerSchool is highly relevant to the node but appears private after Bain acquisition, so it is treated as a coverage gap rather than a candidate.
